newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mostly up in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mostly up in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up in slow trading on Tuesday due to speculative buying by retail investors, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at 3,202 yuan ($385) per tonne, losing 26 yuan. It opened at 3,202 and stayed at that level for the whole session.
March rose four yuan to 3,244, May 28 to 3,328, July 10 to 3,370, September fell 10 to 3,350 and November rose 40 to 3,400.
Combined volume fell to 11,150 tonnes from 12,500.
Traders said speculative buying from retail investors pushed prices up despite an uncertain short-term market trend.
"Retail investors dominated today's trading, with no institutions entering the market because of poor fundamentals," one trader said.
"Soybean will meet hedge-selling at high levels," he added.
The price of spot soybean is around 3,200 yuan per tonne.
Analysts expect soybean to stay in a narrow range in the next few days.
